recipes.name: Classic Spanish Sangria
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup white sugar, or to taste

steps.text: Refrigerate orange, lemon, lime, wine, rum, and orange juice until cold.
Slice orange, lemon, and lime into thin rounds. Place in a large glass pitcher. Add rum and sugar. Refrigerate to allow flavors to blend, about 2 hours.
Crush fruit lightly with a wooden spoon. Stir in wine and orange juice. Adjust sweetness as desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Spanish Sangria
raw_recipe.description: This fruity sangria makes a tangy-sweet cocktail. Add different fruits to make it season-specific, like apples or pears for fall or berries for summer.

review.reviewBody: I let the fruit soak in the rum and an added 1/2 cup of Triple Sec. I made this with a Merlot (Little Penguin) and with a Blackberry Merlot. It was a lot sneakier when it was made with the Blackberry Merlot, i.e. we got drunk, but it hit us from out of no where. When it was made with the Little Penguin Merlot, it was a little too alcoholic. I solved this by having friends who are alcoholics and don't mind.

YesYesYes!!! I was so nervous about making a good sangria for the 1st time during our Covid lockdown Easter and it was AWESOME!! Not a large gathering for Easter, but my husband, and my 2 adult kids that are here and I were thrilled how delicious this turned out. 
• Used the Kraken Spiced Rum • made a 1/4C simple syrup bc some comments said sugar was a little hard to dissolve • Added all kinds of fruit, including frozen mixed fruit to soak over night • Next morning added fresh fruit • Topped each glass with a splash of ginger ale
We tasted it right when I made it and ?? whew! A kick!! But by the next day this drink tasted like the BEST sangria, and I knew immediately I should have made more lol!! Will be remaking this recipe real soon!!

Super useful! Really glad my cousin introduced me to this website. I did make a couple of changes in terms of the fruits used.

2 Limes
2 Plums
1 Apple
1 Lemon
1 Orange
1 Pear
6 Strawberries
20 Blueberries
12 Raspberries
10 Grapes

I washed them all, cut them thinly, and placed them in the pitcher. Poured in 1 cup of Rum and 1/2 cup of Sugar, and left it to soak for 2 hours straight in the refrigerator.

After 2 hours, I took them out and added half a bottle of wine followed by a cup of Orange Juice. The end product was just amazing with the Sangria looking blood-maroon in hue. Must try!

This is hands down the best sangria. I soak the fruit in the sugar and dark Mount Gay or Appleton Estate rum overnight, then mix with Spanish Garnacha wine and the juice. Sometimes I use orange-mango juice instead of plain orange. Yummy yummy!!
It was excellent! I used organic cane sugar and melted it with half of the orange juice first. Also used organic orange juice, and citrus fruits.

This was a huge hit at my girls night and party last night. I used two oranges sliced in rounds, a lemon, a lime, three different types of apples, about 25 strawberries sliced, and a pair (I needed to make a huge batch). I put all of the fruit in a container, put about three quarters of a cup of sugar over the fruit, and then added 2 cups of very high-quality spiced rum. I let that soak in the fridge overnight, and then in the morning, I poured about a cup and a half of orange juice and three bottles of wine over the fruit and rum mixture. I let that sit in the fridge for another couple of hours before the party. I served it with ice on the side, and everyone loved it. Couldn't get enough of it!! Because of the high quality rum, no one has a headache today either. :-)

When I first read about rum in sangria, I thought no way! But I did it with CM Spiced Rum, strawberries, raspberries, oranges, pears, pineapple. Soaked it for about a day and a half. Added no sugar, and the wine and OJ. It was a big hit! I will definitely make it again. The only thing is you have to plan in advance. I used to make sangria with only red wine and OJ, plus the fruit and I thought THAT was good! LOL, thanks for a great simple recipe!

I’ve been using this recipe since 2010 for my parties, which are at least 2 to 3 times a year. I triple it and sometimes quadruple it, if you do that, just add the sugar gradually as it can get too sweet quickly. You can use rum or brandy depending on the flavor you like. Just don’t add too much Citrus, it can get better because of the rind of the citrus. It is a beautiful punch, and I always have to tell people to be careful as it’s powerful. I always have club soda or sparkling water besides the punch dispenser, for people who want to cut it down. Ice works too. I was counting the parties I’ve had using this punch, and I think I’m about 15 or 16, it’s a go to recipe. I live in Florida, and I often have Cubans, and or Puerto Ricans at my parties, they always say that this is an “authentic “sangria. They love it. I’ll even transported this recipe to other parties in pitcher with lids. It travels very well. Just be sure to put it on the floor of the back seat. Due to open container laws.

I made this recipe for thanksgiving. I let the fruit and the sugar soak in the rum for about 6 hours. I used white rum and added an apple for little extra flavor. It was really good. Everyone enjoyed it. This is a very easy recipe that i will make again.

I made this for an outdoor party; it was super-easy and everyone enjoyed it. I used blackberry merlot and spiced rum. I misread the recipe and thought it called for only 1/2 cup of rum … I actually used 3/4 cup and that was plenty, especially since I now see a lot of reviewers are complaining that the rum is overpowering. Also, in my opinion this doesn't need any sugar at all. So 4 stars because of too much rum and sugar, but after cutting back on those ingredients I would give it 5 stars. Also, I made ice cubes with fruit-flavored sparkling water to keep the mixture cold without diluting the flavor too much.
I loved this! However, I let it marinate in the fridge for 12 hours and did not add the sugar. (I don't like overly sweet drinks). It was delicious!

My book club loved this on our Mexican food night! Every drop disappeared. I made it with Rioja, white rum and added some thinly sliced Granny Smith apple. Delish, but it does pack a little punch, so I warned everyone first!
This recipe made me black out but I slept like a baby

I followed the recipe exactly as listed... but I did use dark rum instead of clear because dark is what I drink and what I had. It came out great, but as others have indicated, it is rather potent. So pace yourself. I used inexpensive red wine (Bigfoot I think) and I combined merlot and cab.
I made this with Coyote Moons, NY Twisted Sister and cut the sugar in half and it was amazing!
Love it. This packs quite a punch!
I made this as written 2 different times with 2 different red wines as written and one without sugar and it was disgusting. Would never recommend this recipe.

Amazing! I did tweak it to my liking tho. Who knew that this amount of rum would’ve worked so well? Anyways I’ve come to the realization that it does not matter what kind of wine you use!! Sweet, dry, red or white! Use whatever but just adjust the sugar content to your liking. I also added Cointreau, grenadine & 7up! Great!

Exactly what I was hoping for on a humid afternoon. I did change it up just a tad, I was concerned about it being overly boozy because of other reviewers. I added a can of sparkling water just to try to thin it a touch. Seemed to help. Also added a little less sugar just because I ran out. This is fab and sweet and refreshing.
